dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: sarvataḥ svaśarīrasya dvādaśānte manolayāt | dṛḍhabuddher dṛḍhībhūtaṃ tattvalakṣyam pravartate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: When the mind dissolves in the dvādaśānta while one's whole body is pervaded (by awareness), the reality that is the goal becomes steadily present for one whose understanding is firm.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh admits it is not clear which bodily dvādaśānta is meant (there are several twelve-finger spans in the body) and suggests the brahmarandhra at the top of the head; Ānandabhaṭṭa's commentary allows the cosmic void or the central channel. Wallis: the dvādaśānta of one's subtle body. Bäumer's version instead reads 'the body is void in all parts'.
dharana.instruction: Fill the body with awareness, then let the mind rest and dissolve at the crown.

The Mystery Within (2019), parallel translations: 'Dharana 27 • verso 50' (agrees)

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 50: Mindfulness of the dvādaśānta (Y24 ~ A2)

source_disagreements: Which dvādaśānta: Singh is unsure (probably the brahmarandhra); Ānandabhaṭṭa allows the cosmic void or the central channel; Bäumer reads the line differently ('the body is void in all parts').

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 50 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the whole body, pervaded by awareness
the dvādaśānta (commentarial: at the crown or just above it)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the whole body filled with awareness, with the mind resting and dissolving at one point at or above the crown.
geometry.svg_hint: a softly filled body outline with a small open point at the crown
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Dissolve at the top
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the mind spreads through the body, then settles and dissolves at one point. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Fill the body with awareness, then rest at the crown
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The whole body pervaded by awareness
attention.secondary: The mind resting and dissolving at the dvādaśānta at or above the crown

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When the mind dissolves in the dvādaśānta while one's whole body is pervaded (by awareness), the reality that is the goal becomes steadily present for one whose understanding is firm.
adiyogi.method_summary: Let awareness fill the whole body. Then let the mind rest at a point at the crown or just above it, and let it dissolve there. Keep the understanding steady; return to the point whenever the mind wanders.

honesty.disclosure: Door 027 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 27 (verse 50) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 027 is dharana 27, verse 50. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).

The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep the attention at the crown light; if pressure or headache appears, move attention to the feet. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Orientation

beats.title: Breath

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Let awareness fill the body. Then rest the mind at the crown, or just above it, and let it dissolve there.

beats.title: Reaction cue
